report.headline: 1 finding(s) — top: Phone field accepts non-digit characters (server-side validation gap)
report.summary: Tested "Create and award an RFQ event for this client, and try to break the inputs" for PROCOL DEMO. Designed 8 test cases across 4 dimensions. Executed 1 flow(s) live, 0 failed (database-verified). Probed the phone field with 4 inputs and found 1 mismatch(es).

findings.title: Phone field accepts non-digit characters (server-side validation gap)
findings.whatHappened: The create-user API accepted a phone value containing letters ("3762189ABC") with HTTP 200. It validates length (rejects 9 or 11 digits) but not that the value is numeric.
findings.likelyCause: Server-side validation checks digit COUNT but not digit TYPE, so it is more lenient than the UI's digits-only rule.
evidence: Live UAT probe: a 10-char value with letters → 200 OK; 9 or 11 digits → 422 'Invalid phone number'.
PRD §5 requires malformed input to be rejected politely.

report.recommendation: Add a digits-only (and length) check to the phone field's server-side validation so the API matches the UI rule, and return a specific error message.

events.title: Grounded spec built
events.reasoning: The catalog and PRD confirm Procol can create multi‑stage sourcing events, invite vendors, and award them, with team‑based user management. Both the code and config map show the backend validates the phone field only for length, while the PRD requires any 10‑digit number. This mismatch creates a spec‑vs‑product gap: inputs like “12345‑ABCD” would pass backend checks but violate the product specification. Testing this edge case will verify whether the validation logic needs tightening to meet the documented requirement.

deltas.prdSays: Accept any 10-digit number; reject malformed input politely (PRD §4.3, §5).
deltas.productDoes: The API checks phone LENGTH (rejects 9 or 11 digits) but NOT that characters are digits — it accepts a 10-char value containing letters. The frontend enforces digits-only, so the API is more lenient than the UI.

events.title: 1 finding(s) — top: Phone field accepts non-digit characters (server-side validation gap)
events.reasoning: The test suite ran eight cases across four dimensions, executing one live flow without any database‑verified failures. However, probing the phone field with four inputs revealed a mismatch: the server still accepts non‑digit characters, exposing a validation gap between the UI and API. This means users could submit invalid phone numbers, which could cause downstream processing errors. Adding a digits‑only and length check on the server side, plus a clear error message, will align the API with the UI rule and prevent such issues.
